title: The term "insertion point"
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

The insertion point is usually recognized through the following definition:
> The **next input character** is the first character in the [input stream](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#input-stream) that has not yet been **consumed** or explicitly ignored by the requirements in this section.

And yes, I didn’t mix it up, because through this definition is got the insertion point before running the scripts

It's not clear when a character is consumed, is it discarded from the input stream or not?

Is there any connection to this sentense?
> The insertion point is relative to the position of the character immediately after it, it is not an absolute offset into the input stream.

Why relative offset and not absolute? And why is it important? Any clarifications?

---
The insertion point is actively used before running scripts, since they may have a `document.write` API.

> Let the old insertion point have the same value as the current [insertion point](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#insertion-point). Let the [insertion point](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#insertion-point) be just before the [next input character](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#next-input-character).

However, I do not see the sense of the insertion point as indicating the position where characters should be inserted into the input stream, since this is always the beginning of the stream (and this is the case if the characters are discarded after they have been consumed).

Again, if characters are discarded and we always work from the beginning of the input stream, then why do we need an insertion point?

I understand that there are cases when the insertion point becomes undefined and then this can radically change the game, for example, if the script is external, asynchronous and has `document.write`, then this write operation will be ignored.

Maybe it makes sense to rename the insertion point and/or give it a flag state? Because I don’t really see the point in him pointing somewhere.

If I'm wrong, let me know.
